newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour determined to end EU farm subsidies.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour determined to end EU farm subsidies.

text.p: Labour Party leader Tony Blair on Thursday promised that reform of farm policy would be one of his party's key European Union priorities as the party published radical plans to phase out intervention buying and export subsidies.
Agriculture spokesman Gavin Strang said a situation in which a few British farmers received arable payments from Brussels of over 500,000 stg a year had to be put right.

"It is a scandal. Even against the background of the BSE (mad cow disease) crisis, land prices in East Anglia increased 30 percent last year," he said. East Anglia contains some of Britain's largest arable farms.
In a policy document, Strang said the EU should make direct payments to farms which would otherwise suffer unacceptable hardships as EU prices were brought down to world market levels.
He also called for an end to land set-aside which he said was costing rural jobs.

In a preface to the document, Blair, widely expected to become Britain's Prime Minister after an upcoming general election, wrote "If elected we will push ahead with CAP (Common Agricultural Policy) reform as one of our key priorities in Europe."
Strang said the last Labour government, in which he was a junior agriculture minister, had made some progress over CAP reform, although not enough.
He criticised the Conservatives for having made no serious attempt to follow this up over the last 17 years during which they have been in government.
He said there was now a "golden opportunity" to press for reform as the CAP would have to change before more member states were admitted into the EU.
"We know that we will have to get rid of these export subsidies," Strang said.
